$comment: Canonical cross-platform design tokens — the single source of truth for the palette, control geometry, radii and type scale shared by web (apps/web/src/styles.css), Android (Compose), iOS (SwiftUI), and the desktop app (Rust/gpui). The `palette` colors are authored as OKLCH to mirror the web theme verbatim; scripts/generate.ts converts them to sRGB hex for the native targets so the palette is never hand-transcribed. Run `bun run --filter @exp/design-tokens generate` after editing.

semantic.$comment: Fixed semantic accent colors for status/priority/due-date. Not derived from the neutral surface palette; authored as sRGB hex and shared so iOS/Android/desktop stop each carrying their own copy. EXP-594 retired the indigo `brand`/`brandStrong` interaction accent — the main scheme is white/glass (`palette.primary` for solid fills that carry text, the `glass` fills/strokes for selections); these colors are STATUS semantics, plus the `code*` trio: the inline-code tint of the agent CHAT feeds (EXP-698 round 3 — steer bubbles, plan/ask cards, narration; never the issue/comment renderers).

glass.$comment: Glass surface system (EXP-269), transcribed verbatim from the canonical mobile look (apps/ios/ExpUI/Sources/GlassTheme.swift, ported 1:1 to apps/android/.../ui/theme/Glass.kt). A zinc-950→900 page gradient with white-alpha fills and hairline strokes layered on top. Every client reads them through its generated file (iOS ExpUI GlassTokens.swift, Android ui/theme/Glass.kt aliases, desktop tokens.generated.rs, web styles.css --glass-* vars, parity-tested); the styleguide Components group renders the same values (EXP-698).

radius.$comment: Web --radius is 12px; sm/md/lg/xl/xl2/xl3 mirror Tailwind's calc()-derived rounded-sm…3xl steps, which land on the mobile glass ladder (row 10 / section 12 / card 16 / sheet 24). xl2/xl3 because 2xl/3xl are not valid identifiers in the native targets.

size.$comment: Control geometry in px/dp. Web button heights h-9/h-8/h-6 = 36/32/24; input h-9 = 36; list rows h-8 = 32.

motion.$comment: Motion system (EXP-523) — the shared duration/easing vocabulary. THREE durations, stored as integer MILLISECONDS: `fast` for hover/opacity micro-feedback, `standard` for the great majority of enter/exit, expand/collapse and position changes, `slow` for large-surface transitions (nav pushes, sheets, docks). All three are values already proven in this repo (120 web editor chrome, 180 Android `tween(180)` ≡ iOS `.snappy(0.18)`, 280 Android nav) and each step is ~1.5x the last, so they stay perceptually distinct; the stray 200ms sites collapse onto `standard`. THREE easings, authored as CSS cubic-bezier control points [x1, y1, x2, y2] with P0 = (0,0) and P3 = (1,1) implicit — the ONE form all four targets accept: web `cubic-bezier()`, Compose `CubicBezierEasing`, SwiftUI `Animation.timingCurve`, desktop `theme::motion::ease`. `standard` is the default for anything that both enters and leaves, `decelerate` for things arriving, `accelerate` for things leaving. The group is named `ease`, NOT `easing`: in Kotlin a nested `object Easing` self-shadows the Compose `Easing` type. Each target converts the durations itself (Swift seconds, Rust u64 millis for `Duration::from_millis`, Compose ms verbatim, web `<n>ms`). Web is NOT generated — the `--motion-*` vars in apps/web/src/styles.css are hand-authored and parity-tested by apps/web/src/lib/design-tokens.test.ts, exactly like the palette. AMBIENT LOOPS ARE NOT TOKENS: the repeating status pulses (iOS 0.65/0.9/1.4s, Android 650/900ms, web `animate-ping`) are a different design axis and deliberately stay hardcoded at their call sites. Every client reads these through a hand-written reduce-motion wrapper (ExpUI/Sources/Motion.swift, ui/theme/Motion.kt, the `motion-reduce:` variant, crates/theme/src/motion.rs) — never directly.
